about: The slash palette's sizes on a big screen: the category and list columns for a palette so wide (columnWidths, with the detail kept at least 200, the list 120 and the categories 110), its height for a window, and the sizes and column widths a drag leaves. Copies: desktop/core/src/slash.rs (column_widths, palette_height, PaletteLayout) and SlashPalette in ios/ThreadbearKit/Sources/ThreadbearKit/SlashCommands.swift. Android's palette is a sheet with none of this.

cases.name: wide: each column as wide as it needs
wide, as the desktop sizes it
a very long name takes at most half of what's left
narrow: the list gives way first
narrower: then the categories
narrowest: both at their least
a list dragged wide isn't held to half
the same width not dragged is held to half
height: about half the window
height: half of a middling window
height: never below the least
height: nor above the most
dragged height: never too short to use
dragged height: never past 85% of the window
dragged height: as dragged
dragged height: 220 even in a short window
dragged width: never under 480
dragged width: never past the window less 40 a side
dragged width: never past a smaller window less 40 a side
dragged width: 480 when the margins don't fit
dragged width: a window narrower than 480 keeps 8 a side

differs.ios: The Swift palette keeps 480 even off a window too narrow for it; the desktop app keeps 8 in from each side (as its undragged width does). The iPhone never drags its palette, so this only mattered on the frozen Mac app.

cases.name: dragged width: just over 480 keeps 8 a side
